previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with idiopathic chronic pancreatitis was admitted with severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back and nausea, consistent with an acute flare. She was managed with bowel rest, IV fluids, analgesia, and antiemetics. Her course was complicated by aspiration pneumonia, diagnosed on chest X-ray, and treated with a six-day course of levofloxacin and metronidazole. Due to persistent pain with oral intake, TPN was initiated via a left basilic vein PICC line placed on hospital day 6. Her symptoms improved with TPN, and she was discharged home with ongoing TPN, strict NPO status aside from sips and medications, and plans for outpatient follow-up with GI and PCP. Weekly lab monitoring was arranged.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ female with a past medical history of idiopathic 
chronic pancreatitis, depression, and GERD presenting from 
outside epigastric pain radiating to the back and nonbloody, 
nonbilious emesis x 5 days now resolving after pain/nausea 
control now tolerating clear liquids with TPN support.  

# Acute on Chronic pancreatitis - On admission, lipase was 
normal, though can be normal in chronic pancreatitis. Location 
and quality of pain was consistent with an exacerbation of her 
chronic pancreatitis. Her last MRCP in ___ demonstrated mild 
beading and irregularity of the pancreatic duct with mild 
parenchymal atrophy c/w chronic pancreatitis. However, there was 
no evidence of acute inflammatory change, fluid collections, or 
other sequelae of chronic pancreatitis. She slowly improved 
throughout her admission with mosly supportive care including 
TPN administration per nutrition consult reccs, and symptomatic 
pain/nausea control (dilaudid 3mg IV q3h PRN and IV zofran 8mg 
PRN). She was able to be transitioned to PO pain (dilaudid 
___ PO q4h PRN) and nausea medications (Zofran 8mg PO PRN) on 
hospital day 6 (___). Her labs were monitored and she did 
not exhibit any complications of chronic pancreatitis.    

#Anemia: Had been mentioned multiple times in previous notes. 
Likely nutritional and could be component of anemia of chronic 
disease. Per nutrition, sent off some labs as patient is on 
chronic TPN. B12 level borderline low (MCV is 79), folate 
normal, triglycerides normal and other serum electrolytes 
pending (Copper/Thiamine/Zinc). CBCs remained stable while 
admitted. She was started on B12 supplementation, would consider 
Fe supplementation as an outpatient. 
 
# Depression - Chronic, stable. Was continued on home bupropion 
and home sertraline.  

# GERD - Chronic. Did have a few episodes of reflux feelings 
despite continueation of home pantoprazole and ranitidine. 
Required a few PRN doses of Maalox with good relief. EKG normal 
at the time.   

# Overactive bladder - Chronic, remained stable. Continued on 
home oxybutinin while at home.

# Impacted cerumen- Had some ear fullness and tenderness, 
impacted cerumen noted to right ear. Debrox drops used with plan 
to ___ with PCP for removal or referral to ENT. Instructed not 
to continued trying to extract herself with wire loop or 
otherwise.
